data.title: Good Pretraining, Bad SFT: Checkpoint Quality Across the Training Stack
data.description: arXiv:2609.08966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language-model checkpoints are commonly selected by pretraining loss or benchmark scores, assuming that the highest-scoring checkpoint will remain the best starting point for subsequent training. We show that this assumption can fail in a full 30B mixture-of-experts training pipeline. The checkpoints that perform better after the full downstream training stack also have higher solution density, i.e., retain downstream performance under local weight perturbations.
data.author: Sohir Maskey, Philipp Scholl, Jonas Knupp, Pit Neitemeier, Sascha Wirges
